subject: Generate simulated data from Stan file?

messages.author: 49e107cb0f8a3d27
messages.subject: Generate simulated data from Stan file?
parts:
Is there a way to generate simulated data from a Stan file? E.g., I specify hyperparameters from the data block, follow the data generating process from the model block, and dump all the latent variables and observations from the DGP into a file.

My current workflow for testing fits on simulated data is to write the Stan model, and then to write a similar version in R in order to generate the data and stan_rdump things.

Dustin

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: Generate simulated data from Stan file?
parts:
On Saturday, October 17, 2015 at 3:20:27 PM UTC-4, Dustin Tran wrote:
Is there a way to generate simulated data from a Stan file? E.g., I specify hyperparameters from the data block, follow the data generating process from the model block, and dump all the latent variables and observations from the DGP into a file.

My current workflow for testing fits on simulated data is to write the Stan model, and then to write a similar version in R in order to generate the data and stan_rdump things.

You can specify the argument algorithm = "Fixed_param" to stan() to do this, possibly with iter = 1.

Ben

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: Generate simulated data from Stan file?
parts:
This is something we need to write up --- the whole
process for doing this kind of thing.

I tend to do the simulations in R myself. You can
use Stan's generated quantities block to do pure simulation
(simple Monte Carlo, not MCMC).

In some ways, having to write it twice gives a kind of
unit-testing flavor to it. This is one of the cases
where having a directed graphical model without declared
data and parameters would make it easy to simulate and
estimate from the same model.

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Generate simulated data from Stan file?
parts:
Andrew --- I think we're talking about two different things.
I understand we need the new generated quantities thing to
work on a whole sample (everyone else --- I'm going to write
something that lets you write a generated quantities block that
will apply to an existing sample to generate the generated quantities
after the main iterations for sampling).

What I'm talking about here is a way to generate a single fake data
set to use as input to Stan to make sure my program is doing the
right hting. Right now, there's no easy way (that I know of) to convert
Stan output (in any interface) into something that can be fed back in directly
as data.

- Bob

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Generate simulated data from Stan file?
parts:
You need fixed_param as an option so as not to try to sample or
optimize. It's an alternative way to run Stan that just reads in the
data and inits (or randomly inits), sets the parameters to the init values, then
executes the transformed parameter and generated quantities blocks.
So the parameters remained fixed every iteration. And then iter=1 is to
just get a single draw.

- Bob

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Generate simulated data from Stan file?
parts:
You are never going to be able to simulate the design matrix
without giving it a distribution---if it's just covariates,
there's nothing to simulate from. Usually the covariates don't
get modeled because everything's conditionally independent given
their value.

Which interface are you using?

- Bob
